newsitem.title: DUBAI: Sharjah air cargo volumes up 40 percent in July.
newsitem.headline: Sharjah air cargo volumes up 40 percent in July.

text.p: Sharjah airport said cargo volumes rose 40 percent in July to 36,790 tonnes from 26,235 tonnes in the same month last year.
The figure was also higher than June's 30,494 tonnes.

Most of the July total came from transferred freight of 13,378 tonnes. This reflects the hubbing operations of airlines such as Lufthansa Cargo, where cargo is often brought in on one aircraft and transferred to another.
Exports from Sharjah in July totalled 13,063 tonnes.
Among the main destinations were Moscow, which took about 3,356 tonnes, Kandahar in Afganistan with 1,385 tonnes and Tashkent with 868 tonnes.
Some 742 tonnes of exports from Sharjah were destined for Baku, 677 tonnes went to Sochi and 504 tonnes went to Nalchik in southern Russia.
Frankfurt received 501 tonnes and Almaty took 460 tonnes.
The emirate imported 1,820 tonnes of goods through its airport in July, versus 1,162 tonnes in June. Freight in transit in the month was 8,529 tonnes.
Sea-air freight exports from the emirate rose almost 10 percent to 3,658 tonnes in July.
There were 1,563 scheduled flights and 959 charter flights in July, versus 1,218 and 943 respectively in the same month last year.
In July, 76,587 passengers passed through Sharjah airport up from 69,709 a year before. - Hilary Gush, Dubai newsroom +9714-626990 - www.racs.com
